events.title: .NET 10 LTS released
events.summary: Microsoft shipped .NET 10 on November 11, 2025 — an LTS release with AI building blocks, performance gains, and C# 14 through November 2028 support.
events.about: .NET 10 added Microsoft.Extensions.AI abstractions for unified chat clients across OpenAI, Azure, and Ollama — signaling .NET's bet on agentic apps. As the even-year LTS after .NET 9 STS, it became the recommended production baseline for enterprises needing three years of patches.

narrative.whyChosen: .NET 10 paired LTS stability with first-class AI service abstractions.
narrative.whyImportant: IChatClient and vector data APIs made multi-provider AI a platform primitive.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams on .NET 8 LTS needed modern AI APIs without jumping to short-term STS releases.

events.title: OpenAI GPT-5.1 released
events.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5.1 on November 12, 2025 — splitting ChatGPT into warmer Instant and adaptive Thinking tiers with improved instruction-following.
events.about: GPT-5.1 refined the unified GPT-5 stack with personality tuning and faster simple-task routing in Thinking mode. Codex-Mini and Codex-Max variants followed within a week — keeping OpenAI competitive as Google prepared Gemini 3 and Anthropic readied Opus 4.5.

narrative.whyChosen: GPT-5.1 was OpenAI's first major GPT-5 refresh with distinct Instant and Thinking modes.
narrative.whyImportant: Adaptive reasoning effort made frontier models feel more conversational by default.
narrative.problemSolved: GPT-5 users wanted warmer chat and smarter routing without picking separate models.

events.title: Google Gemini 3 Pro released
events.summary: Google released Gemini 3 Pro on November 18, 2025 — state-of-the-art reasoning, generative UI, and a Gemini Agent for multi-step tasks in Search and the Gemini app.
events.about: Gemini 3 Pro shipped day-one in Google Search AI Mode and developer tools — Google's answer to GPT-5.1 and the prelude to Antigravity. Generative Interfaces and the Gemini Agent previewed agentic UX inside Google's consumer products, not just APIs.

narrative.whyChosen: Gemini 3 Pro launched Google's agentic era in Search and the Gemini app simultaneously.
narrative.whyImportant: Generative UI and in-Search deployment raised the stakes for consumer AI distribution.
narrative.problemSolved: Google needed a frontier model that could reason, code, and orchestrate tools in one stack.

events.title: Google Antigravity released
events.summary: Google released Antigravity on November 20, 2025 — an agentic development platform with an AI IDE, autonomous agents across editor, terminal, and browser.
events.about: Antigravity elevated agents to a first-class surface: they plan, execute, and verify tasks while developers steer mid-flight. Built on Gemini 3 Pro with support for Claude Sonnet 4.5 and open models, it competed directly with Cursor, Copilot, and Claude Code for the agentic IDE market.

narrative.whyChosen: Antigravity made Google a direct player in agent-first developer tooling.
narrative.whyImportant: Browser-and-terminal agents changed IDE design from autocomplete to task orchestration.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers needed AI that could run multi-step engineering work, not just suggest lines.

events.title: Anthropic Claude Opus 4.5 released
events.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.5 on November 24, 2025 — leading SWE-bench Verified coding scores with Excel, Chrome, and desktop integrations at $5/$25 per million tokens.
events.about: Opus 4.5 closed Anthropic's 2025 with the highest public coding benchmark scores and automatic context summarization for long chats. Claude for Excel and Chrome expanded beyond terminals — positioning Anthropic for knowledge-work agents competing with GPT-5.1 and Gemini 3.

narrative.whyChosen: Opus 4.5 set the year's top public coding benchmark for frontier models.
narrative.whyImportant: Spreadsheet and browser integrations pushed Claude into everyday office workflows.
narrative.problemSolved: Enterprise teams needed frontier coding and computer-use in one model at Opus-tier pricing.
